p: The Trafford Centre has grown into a whole leisure district, and that makes it easy to build a full day around SEA LIFE. Plan on a couple of hours for the aquarium itself, with toddlers and pre-schoolers usually happiest at a slow amble and older kids getting more out of the keeper talks and feeding times.

Getting there is simpler than many people expect. The Metrolink tram line to the Trafford Centre means you can leave the car at home and hop on from the city centre, which saves a lot of circling round the car parks on a busy Saturday. Driving is still the most popular option, especially from the M60, but weekends and the run-up to Christmas get very busy.

If your lot have energy left, Chill Factore is close by in Trafford City, with real snow, lessons and snow play for younger children. It's a very different sort of cold to the aquarium. For something free and fascinating, IWM North at Salford Quays is a short drive away, a striking building telling the stories of people caught up in modern conflict, and better suited to older children and grown-ups.
Football fans will know Old Trafford isn't far away either, home to Manchester United and, just up the road, Lancashire's cricket ground. Stadium tours are popular, so book ahead if you fancy one.

A few practical tips make the day go smoothly. Book your aquarium slot for the morning, when it's calmer, then do the shops or other attractions afterwards. Keep a bag with snacks and water to hand, and agree a meeting point in case anyone wanders off in the crowds.
